about.text: Mexico's most popular fresh cheese, also widely eaten in the United States. Skimmed or partly skimmed milk is set with rennet at about 38 °C, and the curd is finely milled before salting, which makes the cheese crumbly. It is pressed only by its own weight, is not ripened and has a short shelf life.

how.label: mill the curd
how.text: The rennet curd is ground fine, salted and packed into moulds instead of being pressed into a solid block, so the cheese stays moist (46–57%) and crumbles. It is eaten unripened, so it tastes of fresh milk and salt.
